text:
viv: quick check-in on model identity + rollout metadata. i'm trying to avoid the classic "name vs hash vs id" bikeshed. proposal: runtime routing uses an opaque `stable_id` as the canonical key, control-plane offers short-lived `session_token` bindings for name pins, and we always publish `manifest_fingerprint` for verification. thoughts? :clipboard:

oscar: i like the separation. runtime only needs stable_id (deterministic), session_token helps clients avoid re-resolving every request. manifest_fingerprint is required for clients that pre-warm artifacts.

mei: important: session_token should carry a remap watermark so we can invalidate in-band without waiting for TTL expiry. don't rely solely on TTLs for emergency remaps.

prio: agree. small proposal on fields: `stable_id`, `manifest_fingerprint`, `session_token`, `token_expires_at`, `remap_watermark`, `fallback_sequence`, and `deprecation_window`. Keep names explicit.

viv: example compact metadata (for RFC text, not nested objects):

```
stable_id=sid-9f1b
manifest_fingerprint=sha256:abcd1234...
session_token=st-20260323-77
token_expires_at=2026-03-23T20:00:00Z
remap_watermark=128
fallback_sequence=stable_id,manifest_fingerprint,compatible_variant,rollback_anchor
deprecation_window=30d
```

oscar: regarding `fallback_sequence` — runtime should treat it as an ordered list and log which fallback path was used. that makes postmortems deterministic. also recommend a `rollback_anchor` field that is an explicit stable_id target for safe rollbacks (no server guessing).

mei: on transport semantics: control-plane should accept name pins but always resolve server-side and return two headers: `X-Effective-Stable-Id` and `X-Session-Token`. clients should cache the token and the effective id. if a request fails with a mismatch we return a specific status header `X-Remap-Watermark` and an HTTP 412 to force re-resolve.

prio: +1. also add `X-Manifest-Fingerprint` in the response so on-prem SDKs verify before loading large blobs. if fingerprint mismatches, return 409 with guidance.

viv: on migration: we can't break customers that pin by name/semver. migration plan sketch: 1) catalog publishes stable_id alongside existing names; 2) control-plane auto-resolves legacy name pins and returns session_token + ttl for a grace period; 3) after grace, start returning deprecation warnings (header + metrics) and block new name-pins with an explicit error code unless `force_name_pin=true`.

oscar: ops/rate limits: remap operations must be rate-limited and auditable. we should include `remap_token` in metadata that points to a catalog audit record rather than embedding history in responses. example: `remap_token=rt-20260323-19` so logs can be correlated.

mei: security/ACLs: alias remaps should require a small approval matrix. include `required_signoffs` metadata on remap records (e.g., ["sre","product"]) and surface that in the catalog UI. control-plane rejects remaps without required signoffs for certain alias namespaces.

prio: client behavior pseudocode i'll put in the RFC: 

```
// client bootstrap
if looks_like_stable_id(pin) {
  use(pin)
} else {
  resp = resolveName(pin) // returns X-Effective-Stable-Id, X-Session-Token, ttl
  cache(resp.X-Effective-Stable-Id, resp.X-Session-Token, ttl)
}

// request loop
attach header X-Session-Token
send request
if status == 412 or header X-Remap-Watermark > local.watermark {
  re-resolve immediately
}
if status == 409 and header X-Manifest-Fingerprint != local.fingerprint {
  fail-safe: do not swap large artifacts automatically; alert operator
}
```

viv: good. a few operational constraints: default token_expires_at should be short (e.g., 300s) for public hosted API, longer for dedicated/private with opt-in. session token invalidation must be near-instant for incident-driven remaps via watermark.

oscar: metrics: expose `session_token_invalidations`, `fallback_invocations` (tagged by sequence step), and `manifest_mismatch_rate`. Alert if token invalidations spike or fallback_invocations to emergency fallback exceed threshold.

mei: code/runtime change: routing lookup should prefer `X-Session-Token` -> stable_id if present, then fall back to stable_id param, then manifest_fingerprint-based variant selection, following `fallback_sequence`. record `effective_route` in logs.

prio: one more edge: allow a `binding_mode` flag per catalog entry: {sticky_session, per_request_ephemeral, manual_refresh}. helps SDKs decide caching behavior and operators choose safety level.

viv: action items: (viv) write RFC follow-up with the compact schema, header contract, and migration playbook; (oscar) draft remap audit + rate-limit policy; (mei) prototype server 412/409 semantics and headers; (prio) add runtime metrics & dashboard spec.

infra-bot: note: catalog-service staging now returns `manifest_fingerprint` and `remap_token` on /resolve (feature-flagged).

viv: thanks, closing. will ping when RFC PR is up. :rocket:
